rubric_items.reason: REQ-1 to REQ-4 are all traced by S-1; REQ-2 is noted as a build constraint, and both day-boundary directions and both unchanged targets have criteria.
One story delivering one user-visible outcome, with four criteria.
AC1 and AC2 would fail a UTC-date implementation and AC3 and AC4 cover regression; AC2 gives no concrete zone, instant or date.
AC3 names `timeZone` and `currency`, which the intent does not contain; they come from the ticket, which the artifact does not cite.
Short, clear criteria with consistent terms; the body matches the front matter in substance.

findings.text: AC3 uses field names `timeZone` and `currency` that the intent never states (REQ-4 says only "existing settings fields"). The names match the ticket, but the artifact neither cites it nor derives them.

cites.quote: The existing settings fields and `GET /health` are unchanged.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a claim naming these fields that cites ticket.md#L16 or the product code at the pinned SHA, or word AC3 as the intent does (existing settings fields).

findings.text: AC2 gives no concrete zone, instant or expected date (only "behind UTC" and "previous day"), unlike AC1, so each tester must choose the boundary values.

cites.quote: Given a configured hospital time zone behind UTC and an instant just after midnight in UTC

findings.suggested_fix: State a concrete UTC instant, offset and expected date with the derivation inline, using a zone name only if a cited source supplies one.

cites.quote: computed with the existing day helper in `api/src/lib/time.ts`
